children: The UK unemployment rate was unchanged for the fourth consecutive period at 4.9% in the three months to July 2026, defying expectations that it would rise to 5.0%.

The number of unemployed people rose by 11 thousand from the previous quarter and by 83 thousand year-on-year to 1.778 million, with the annual increase driven by a rise in those unemployed for more than six months.
Meanwhile, total employment rose by 66 thousand from the previous period and by 243 thousand from a year earlier to 34.478 million.
The employment rate was unchanged at 75.1% on the quarter but down 0.1 percentage points from a year earlier.

Both full-time and part-time employment increased from a year earlier, although part-time employment declined in the latest quarter, while the annual increase in full-time employment was driven by more full-time employees and the rise in part-time employment by more part-time self-employed workers.

title: UK Jobless Rate Unexpectedly Holds at 4.9%
